info.title: Fixsure API
info.summary: Photo-verified home-repair escrow on PayPal, for single repairs and crew projects.
info.description:
Fixsure keeps the customer's money as a PayPal authorization (Orders v2, intent AUTHORIZE) and captures it only when a photo proves the work.

**Repairs.** A vision model prices the before photo. The customer places the hold. The technician posts an after photo. If the model finds the same job, a resolved issue, and confidence of at least 0.82, the hold is captured and the technician is paid with PayPal Payouts. Anything else goes to a staff reviewer.

**Projects.** A planning agent splits the request into 2 to 6 milestones, books crew by trade on working days, and sets how each milestone is verified: `ai` up to `MILESTONE_HUMAN_REVIEW_ABOVE_USD` (default $400), `ai_then_human` above it, and `human` for steps a photo cannot prove. One authorization covers the total. Each proven milestone is a partial capture followed by a payout to its crew member. Stopping a project voids whatever is still held.

**Authentication.** Send a key as `Authorization: Bearer <key>`. Each job has a customer key and, for repairs, a technician key. Each crew member has a portal key that only reaches milestones booked to them. Staff endpoints take the server's staff key, or the staff cookie from `POST /api/v1/session` with a same-origin `Origin` header on writes. A key that does not belong to the job gets a 404, so ids cannot be probed.

**Errors** use RFC 9457 `application/problem+json`. Creates return 201 with a `Location` header.

The high-level and low-level design, with diagrams, are in the Design guides of the APIMatic portal and at `/docs/design/hld` and `/docs/design/lld` on any Fixsure server.

post.summary: Create a job from a photo
post.description: Stores the before photo and prices the repair with the vision model. The response is the customer's view, and `links.customer` carries the customer key.

photo.description: JPG, PNG, or WebP under 5 MB.

post.summary: Create the sample faucet job
post.description: Creates a job from the bundled before photo, so the flow can be tried without uploading.

get.description: The shape depends on the caller. Technicians do not see the customer's name, and customers do not see the technician link.

post.summary: Authorize the PayPal hold (customer)
post.description: With PayPal keys, this creates an Orders v2 order with intent AUTHORIZE and answers 202. Send the customer to `hold.approveUrl`; PayPal returns them to `/api/v1/paypal/return`, which authorizes the order. Without keys, the job is funded in demo mode and the answer is 200.

202.description: Waiting for the customer to approve on PayPal.

delete.summary: Cancel the hold before proof is submitted (customer)
delete.description: Voids the PayPal authorization. Not allowed once the technician has uploaded an after photo.

post.summary: Upload the after photo (technician)
post.description: The vision model compares the before and after photos. A passing verdict captures the hold and sends the payout; anything else moves the job to review. An after photo identical to the before photo is rejected.

email.description: PayPal email for the payout. Required when PayPal is connected.

post.description: The same email reuses the PayPal idempotency key, so a payout that went through is never sent twice. A new email is a new payout.

get.description: PayPal redirects the buyer here with `token` (the order id). The server checks that the order belongs to the job and matches the price, authorizes it, and redirects with 303 to the customer's job page.

post.summary: Staff sign-in for the browser desks

204.description: Signed in. Sets an httpOnly `fixsure_staff` cookie.

post.summary: Plan a project into milestones and book crew
post.description: The planning agent (Vercel AI SDK generateObject with the photo) writes 2 to 6 priced milestones. Crew are assigned by trade and least load, laid out on working days, and each milestone gets a verification mode by amount. Without OPENAI_API_KEY a template plan is used.

startDate.description: Earliest start, YYYY-MM-DD. Defaults to tomorrow.

patch.summary: Move, reassign, reprice, or change verification (staff)
patch.description: Only scheduled milestones change. Prices lock once the hold is placed. The Bryntum board sends crewId, startsAt, and endsAt on every drag.

post.summary: Post the photo that proves a milestone (crew)
post.description: ai milestones that pass the check are captured and paid at once. Everything else goes to a person. A photo already used on the project is rejected.

post.summary: Ask the AI dispatch copilot (staff)
post.description: Vercel AI SDK generateText with up to 8 tool steps. Board tools: list_projects, list_crew, reschedule_milestone, assign_milestone, set_verification. With PayPal keys it also gets PayPal Agent Toolkit tools: get_order, list_transactions, create_invoice, send_invoice, list_invoices, get_invoice.

jobKey.description: The customer key or the technician key for one job.

staffCookie.name: fixsure_staff
staffCookie.description: Set by POST /api/v1/session. Writes also need a same-origin Origin header.

crewKey.description: A crew member's portal key. It only reaches milestones booked to that crew member.

JobChecked.description: Proof stored and judged. `status` is `released` or `review`.

Forbidden.description: The credential's role cannot do this.

NotFound.description: No such job for this key.

Conflict.description: The job is in the wrong state for this action.

UnsupportedMedia.description: Wrong content type or image format.

Validation.description: One or more fields are invalid.

Unavailable.description: The feature needs a key this server does not have.

links.description: Page links. `customer` and `technician` carry that role's key in `?k=`.

VerificationMode.description: ai: a passing AI check releases the milestone. ai_then_human: the AI checks, a person approves. human: a person only.

Project.description: Present on milestone projects, null on single repairs.

portalUrl.description: Carries the crew key. Staff only.

workload.description: Returned by GET /api/v1/crew and GET /api/v1/crew/{id}; left out of create and update responses.

Schedule.description: Loads straight into a Bryntum Scheduler: crew as resources, milestones as events.

CrewWorkload.description: What the crew member has on their plate across every project. Cancelled milestones and voided projects are left out.

readyForProof.description: Scheduled milestones on funded projects. The crew member can upload proof for these now.

awaitingHold.description: Scheduled milestones on projects the customer has not funded yet.

inReview.description: Milestones whose proof is waiting on a person.

failedPayouts.description: Paid milestones whose PayPal payout failed, usually a wrong email.

bookedDays.description: Calendar days covered by open (scheduled or in review) milestones.

earnedUsd.description: Sum of payouts that did not fail.
